root.name: Bishop's Opening: Pratt Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 Bc5 3. c3 Nf6 4. d4 exd4 5. e5 d5 6. exf6 dxc4 7. Qh5 O-O

overview: A forcing Philidor-style line where White grabs space with e5, Black counters with ...d5, and after 6.exf6 dxc4 7.Qh5 O-O both sides have taken a minor piece. White's queen eyes c5 and h7; Black's pawn on d4 and bishop on c5 give counterplay. Sharp and tactical; unsure of the theory beyond move 8.

white_ideas.idea: Use the f6 pawn and Qh5 to harass Black's king and the c5 bishop
Win back material and break open Black's kingside

black_ideas.idea: Castle, then take on c3 or play ...Qxf6 to open lines for the pieces
Use the d4/c4 pawn mass and the bishop on c5

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with a White pawn on f6 and Black passed pawns on c4 and d4

character.notes: Both sides took pieces on moves 6 and 7 and the position is full of tactics.

gambit.notes: Pieces were exchanged on move 6; no one gives material that cannot be taken back.

soundness.notes: Believed playable for both; I do not recall a refutation.

structure.notes: Central pawns come off, lines are open for the queen and bishops.

approach.notes: A deep, rare line; strong players seldom reach it.

level.notes: Forcing line with concrete tactics that must be remembered.

character.reason: Forcing exchanges and a queen raid on h5 make the position double-edged.

gambit.reason: Material comes back in the exchanges rather than being offered.

soundness.reason: No clear refutation known for either side.

structure.reason: Central pawns have been traded and lines are open.

approach.reason: A very rare deep line of the Bishop's Opening.

level.reason: Needs some forcing-line recall but is not main-line theory.

plans.reason: Qh5 raid on the king and the early queen.
